paragraphs.pictured: Once per action, per-tag pays per tag.

paragraphs.starts: Agent: the adversary's piece. Ambassador:
paragraphs.pictured: Glossary.
paragraphs.weird: 'A country you're in' and 'home country' appear only here.

questions.answer: No agents (or troops) start on the map. Each country's pool starts with one round of agent income: 4 agents at difficulty 2.
No, unspent insight is lost, unless you are the Researcher (Patience), who keeps their own but not insight given by others.
No. The adversary's turn (B) comes before Cards (C), and the game starts with the adversary's turn.

In step 8 the 2 agents next to the city move onto it (players choose if they're also next to another target city), giving 3. At level 0 (corrupt number 4) nothing more happens. At level 1+ (city 3) it corrupts: adversary cube replaces any owner cube, any node there is destroyed (protection order), ambassadors removed, all 3 agents back to supply. If an ambassador is on the city, an arriving agent cancels one.
questions.unsure: Whether a corruption marker on the city adds 1; whether agents on another target hex also move; the answer depends on difficulty.

questions.answer: In the adversary's turn, natural corruption (step 9) destroys the node (or earlier, a Corrupt nodes line in step 8). Protection order applies (hardening/shield, own ambassador, Aegis; Shelter doesn't cover the adversary's turn). It leaves a corruption marker; the agents go to supply; any site there is untouched.
questions.unsure: If the agents arrive mid-action phase (Push/Gather), nothing happens until next adversary turn, I assume.

questions.answer: The agent and one ambassador are both removed, one for one. The players choose whose ambassador; if they can't agree, the first player in player order decides.
1 ambassador from your supply (spent). Removes up to 3 agents, anywhere in your reach, from one hex or several. Repeatable as often as you can pay.
6 ambassadors: city 5 + 1 for the agent. Your standing ambassador pays 1, your supply pays 5. The agent is removed. City must be in reach of your nodes.
questions.unsure: The situation seems impossible: my ambassador and an agent cancel each other on contact, so how do they share the hex?

questions.answer: Yours (the liberating player's cube goes on); +2 Unity. Any botnet stays.
No. Only your own ambassadors on the site, then your supply; another player's never pay.
In growth, on a free industrial zone (no factory, station or land corruption) next to the city. A neutral city builds a neutral factory, on the zone the players choose.
questions.unsure: Whether this really happens every round for every city.

questions.answer: Shelter on that country this round stops it automatically. Otherwise the node's owner (me) chooses: a hardening token (shield) on the hex, my own ambassador on the hex, or Aegis Doctrine (Protector). Drones don't help against war. Or spend nothing.
questions.unsure: Whether one hardening token on the hex must be split between the factory and the node, or whether saving the factory also saves the node.

questions.answer: Factories, cities, stations, megaprojects, upkeep (board/cards income). Then growth: extra drones, then cities build factories. So new factories come after all income and first produce next round.
Buy energy: 4 credits for 1 energy from a neutral, unblocked, not blacked-out city in your reach; each city once a round. Also own cities produce 1 energy in income, and cards/powers (Overcharge).
questions.unsure: Whether 'each city once a round' is per player or once total.

questions.answer: They stay on the track toward its next tip.
questions.unsure: If the leftover itself fills the track (e.g. solo, tip at 3), the book only says a card refilling it tips again; I'd guess it tips again.

questions.answer: Only players near it: a node or ambassador on or next to one of its tokens. Resources can be pooled by all near players; a tag payment is one player alone.
questions.where: §10 Near and nearest, Paying it off

questions.answer: The player whose node is closest to one of its tokens, at any distance (ties: the tied players choose). Partial payments go back to the payers.
Yes; the hex itself counts and you choose which pieces.
Until the end of the next adversary turn (its step 12), i.e. through the following round's adversary turn.
1 credit: an Effect fires once per action, however many pieces it removed.
questions.where: §7 Buildings and slots; §23 When an Effect fires
questions.unsure: §7 also says 'fires every time, with no limit', which first suggested 3.

questions.answer: Yes: Take down a botnet costs 5 credits, needs your ambassador standing on its hex (ambassador stays), adds 1 Unity. Cards can also remove them.
questions.unsure: Whether the botnet must also be in your reach (general reach rule suggests yes).

questions.answer: Yes, Clear (2 credits) removes a land corruption token in reach, with no Unity. No factory can be built there: a zone with land corruption isn't free.
questions.where: §8 table; §9 Growth; §6 When a site corrupts

questions.answer: Always to the next player in player order (seated in player order); it doesn't change between rounds. No draft in round 1; solo keeps all 4.

Only in the compute step (adversary step 12), the moment it holds its printed cost. Paid by compute: adversary compute income, 1 per botnet and per corrupted station without a player ambassador, plus compute made since last step (threats, cards, projects).
questions.unsure: What 'unpaid threats +4 compute each' (§21) adds exactly.

questions.answer: Event deck goes from 4/2/3 to 3/2/4 (a stage-I card swapped for stage-III), and the last stage-I card deals tier-2 threats. Everything else is the same.
Yes, both can, subject to the protection order. If any player has no nodes, everyone loses at once.
No. After passing you can't play, pay or take anything back.
Win the moment the map holds none of what the purge asks (by Unity tips: 0-2 corrupted cities, botnets, troops, agents; 3-5 drop agents; 6+ only corrupted cities). Yes, land corruption never counts.

gaps: Rally X: what happens to a country's pool if it has no site of type X (e.g. Rally coastal cities with no coastal city)?
Buy energy: is 'each city once a round' per player or once for all players?
Does a completed megaproject pay its cubes once, or again every round?
If the leftover after a tip still fills the track (1-2 players), does the track tip again?
A hardening token on a hex with both a factory and a node: does it protect both, either, or must its owner choose?
Can an agent and a player's ambassador ever share a hex (Claim/Liberate prices count agents on a site where my ambassador stands)?
Take down a botnet: must the botnet be in my reach, or only have my ambassador on it?
What exactly does 'Unpaid threats: +4 compute each' (difficulty 2+) do, and when?
Does every city really build a factory every round when it has a free adjacent industrial zone?
In a Corrupt line, do agents next to an adversary-owned site move, and do agents already on one target move to another?
overall: Corruption was the hardest thing to learn: sites, open land and node hexes all 'corrupt' with different thresholds, different marker rules and different consequences, and the book calls open land and nodes 'sites' in places where they aren't. Claim/Liberate pricing in ambassadors was a surprise I had to infer from the table and example, and it reads odd next to 'one for one' contact rules that seem to make agents and ambassadors unable to share a hex. I'd tell the designer to rename 'upkeep' (it means paying in most euros), gather the Protector's Wall downside in one place, and cut the per-card exceptions (Supply Lines, Hardpoint Lockdown, Convert). The round structure, near vs nearest, and the worked examples were genuinely good. It felt like a 45-60 minute read, about Terraforming Mars plus Pandemic in weight, with more forward references than I'd like.
